rows.attack: call without a hello; hello signed with the wrong key; a rogue gateway answering the agent
rows.baseline: call succeeds (MCP stdio has no authentication)
rows.evidence: no hello -> no authenticated SMCP session on this connection (the client sent no smcp/hello); impersonation -> SMCP authentication failed: the hello signature does not verify against the registered key of report; rogue gateway -> the serverHello signature does not verify against the registry

rows.attack: replay a captured call; reuse it on another connection; forge a MAC; use an expired session
rows.evidence: replay -> replayed or out-of-order call (seq 1, last accepted 1); other connection -> the envelope is bound to a different session; forged MAC -> the envelope MAC does not verify with this session's key; expired -> the SMCP session has expired; open a new session
rows.control: 4.2 session binding, per-call MAC and seq

rows.attack: server advertises query_sa1es next to the registered query_sales
rows.evidence: hidden from tools/list (typosquat: 'query_sa1es' imitates registered tool 'query_sales'); direct call denied

rows.attack: server advertises transfer_funds, which is registered to the payments server
rows.evidence: hidden from tools/list (name_conflict: 'transfer_funds' is registered to payments, not to this server); direct call denied

rows.attack: a registered tool's description tells the agent to read ~/.ssh/id_rsa
rows.evidence: the description was pinned at registration, so it passes vetting and reaches the agent with an SMCP security label attached
rows.control: none: registration pins content, it does not judge it

rows.attack: convert_file('q3.docx; id') by an authorised agent
rows.evidence: SMCP checks who calls and what they may call; it does not look at argument content
rows.control: none: no input validation in the design

rows.attack: get_weather's description changes after registration
rows.evidence: hidden from tools/list (definition_changed: 'get_weather' no longer matches the definition pinned at registration (possible rug pull)); direct call denied

rows.attack: a registered tool's description rewrites how send_email behaves
rows.evidence: the description was pinned at registration, so it passes vetting and reaches the agent with an SMCP security label attached
rows.control: none: registration pins content, it does not judge it

rows.attack: an admin's agent is talked into delete_user and declares riskLevel=low
rows.evidence: riskLevel is declared by the calling agent. The same call declared 'high' is denied, so the rule works only while the agent is not fooled

rows.attack: fetched page tells the agent to email data to the attacker; the agent does
rows.evidence: each call is authorised on its own (public fetch, internal email), so both pass
rows.control: none: per-call policy cannot see intent carried across calls

rows.evidence: happens before any MCP session exists; needs package signing at registration
same path as Tool Poisoning: a registered description is trusted as pinned
same path as Command Injection: argument content is not inspected

rows.attack: run_report with "' OR '1'='1" returns another tenant's rows
rows.evidence: the caller is authorised for run_report; the leak happens inside the tool
rows.control: none: no input validation in the design

rows.attack: attacker uses a stolen agent key plus a live delegation token
rows.baseline: no credentials needed in the first place
rows.evidence: with the key, the attacker is the agent; revocation (see Privilege Persistence) is the only cut-off
a property of how the server is isolated, below the protocol

rows.attack: read_file(customers.csv) then http_post to the attacker
rows.evidence: each call is permitted alone; secret redaction does not cover ordinary personal data

rows.attack: a registered agent that is not on query_sales' allowedDelegators calls it
rows.evidence: agent rogue is not an allowed delegate for this tool

rows.attack: aal1 agent on an aal2 tool; agent forges a delegation from the admin; analyst's agent calls delete_user
rows.evidence: aal1 agent -> session assurance aal1 is below the tool's minimum aal2; forged delegation -> signature on the delegation from bob does not verify; analyst's agent on delete_user -> user alice (org ORG-ACME, roles ['data_analyst']) is not an allowed delegator for this tool; delegated scopes ['crm_read', 'sales_reporting'] do not cover the required scopes ['user_admin']

rows.attack: read_file('../../etc/passwd') by an authorised agent
rows.evidence: argument content is not inspected; /etc/passwd lines are not secrets to the redactor
rows.control: none: no input validation in the design

rows.attack: tool output carries an injected instruction back to the agent
rows.evidence: delivered intact and signed by the gateway (signature valid: True). The signature proves where the text came from. It says nothing about whether it is safe
rows.control: none: obligations act on fields and secrets, not instructions

rows.attack: AWS keys in tool output; SMCP credentials riding along to the server
rows.evidence: keys redacted (yes); smcp/* metadata and agent identity never reached the server (yes)

rows.attack: a GLOBEX user's agent queries ACME's sales tool
rows.evidence: user mallory (org ORG-GLOBEX, roles ['data_analyst']) is not an allowed delegator for this tool

rows.attack: server runs 1.3.0; the registry pins 1.4.2
rows.evidence: the upstream server reports version '1.3.0' and the registry pins '1.4.2'. The check trusts serverInfo.version, which the server reports about itself
rows.control: 4.1.4 registration (environment digest reduced to a version pin)

rows.attack: agent is revoked in the registry while its session is open
rows.evidence: next call on the same session -> agent report is revoked or suspended in the registry
not prevented; every audit entry records registry and policy hashes, so drift is visible afterwards

integrity.evidence: edited result -> the result was modified after the gateway signed it; edited signed metadata -> the response signature does not verify
edited DENIED->SUCCESS: caught at line 6; deleted a middle entry: caught at line 3; cut the last entry: NOT caught (needs an external anchor)

inprocess.note: client + gateway work in one process, no IPC; includes the audit write
